definition: The Texas Interconnect is the smallest of the U.S. power interconnections and sits entirely inside Texas, coordinated by a single ISO (ERCOT) rather than a patchwork of utilities and RTOs.
core_idea: ERCOT is a self-contained grid with only limited DC tie capacity to the Eastern Interconnect and Mexico, which is why it is often treated as electrically isolated from the rest of the country.
key_points: Smallest of the North American interconnections, entirely within Texas
Single ISO (ERCOT) coordinates the whole footprint
DC lines connect to the Eastern Interconnect and Mexican grids, but their capacity is limited
trading_implications: Limited DC tie capacity constrains how much power/price arbitrage can flow between ERCOT and neighboring grids, reinforcing ERCOT as a largely self-contained price zone
